html:
Elizabeth I was Queen of England and Ireland from 1558 to 1603, the last of the Tudor monarchs. She settled England's Protestant church, saw off the Spanish Armada in 1588 and gave her name to the Elizabethan age of Shakespeare.

She was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn, who was beheaded when Elizabeth was two. Under her Catholic half sister Mary she was briefly held in the Tower of London. She became queen at 25.

Her reign:

  • The religious settlement of 1559 made a Protestant Church of England with the queen as its Supreme Governor, broad enough for most of the country to accept.
  • She never married, using the chance of marriage as a tool of foreign policy.
  • Her Catholic cousin, Mary, Queen of Scots, was held captive for nineteen years and executed in 1587 after plots to put her on the throne.
  • In 1588 the Spanish Armada, sent by Philip II of Spain, was beaten by English ships and storms.
  • Sea captains such as Francis Drake raided Spanish shipping, and the East India Company was chartered in 1600.

Her later years brought war in Ireland, bad harvests and money troubles. But the age also produced Shakespeare, Marlowe and Spenser, and her own image as Gloriana was carefully built through portraits and pageants.

She died in 1603 without children, and the crown passed to James VI of Scotland, Mary's son, uniting the two crowns that England and Scotland would later merge.
sum: Elizabeth I was Queen of England and Ireland from 1558 to 1603, the last of the Tudor monarchs. She settled England's Protestant church, saw off the Spanish Armada in 1588 and gave her name to the Elizabethan age of Shakespeare.
